CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain in knees.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis who presents with bilateral knee pain. The patient reports that over the weekend while moving boxes up and down basement stairs, he developed bilateral knee pain that was equally severe. He denies any specific injury but notes he has had knee problems in the past. He attributes the current pain to repetitive activity and the weight of the boxes. The pain was severe enough to keep him up Saturday night. He has tried acetaminophen and ice with minimal relief. He denies associated fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. The pain has impacted his sleep but he has not provided specific details about limitation of activities of daily living.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headaches. Reports occasional elbow pain but notes this is not out of the ordinary. Otherwise, review of systems is negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (several years ago for polycystic kidneys)
Hypothyroidism
Arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications (patient reports taking as prescribed)
Levothyroxine (Synthroid) - taking regularly

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports moving boxes up and down basement stairs over the weekend, which precipitated current knee pain.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Within normal limits, no fever. Heart rate and blood pressure normal.
Cardiovascular: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted on heart exam, stable compared to prior exams.
Knees: Right knee with edema and erythema, pain to palpation, and decreased range of motion. Left knee appears normal.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment, no acute fracture.
Laboratory: White blood cell count not elevated. Kidney function very good.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute knee pain/Acute exacerbation of arthritis: Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Patient advised to take it easy. If symptoms continue, will consider further imaging and possible referral to physical therapy.

2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Ordered thyroid panel.

3. Arthritis: Continue current management. Discussed limitations with anti-inflammatory medications due to kidney transplant status. Will reassess over the next couple weeks and refer to physical therapy if needed.
